definitions: A lawyer in England and Wales who has been called to the bar and is qualified to plead in the higher courts.
A member of one of the two classes of lawyers (barristers and solicitors) in England and Wales, who has the right to argue cases in the higher courts.
examples: She decided to become a barrister.
The barrister presented the case to the judge.
He consulted a barrister for legal advice.
